current_example.problem:
The figure below shows the graph of $f(x).$ What is $\lim_\limits{x \to \,-\,4} f(x)?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227428/assets/ab2abe13314c2005907dcd5d7077af8e87b7126474bbb0261f757d8ec7c00698.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
As $x$ approaches $-4$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ grows to infinity, and therefore

$$
\lim_\limits{x\to -4^+} f(x)=\infty.
$$

However, the function $f(x)$ is not defined for $x<-4,$ and consequently we cannot approach $x=-4$ from the left. So we have

$$
\lim_\limits{x\to -4^-} f(x)=\text{DNE},
$$

and therefore

$$
\lim_\limits{x\to -4} f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$
